author: WP04
summary: Explains where CNA's C++ value layout departs from XNA's value types (Color's vtables and 24-byte size, IVertexType, the internal vertex-stream structs), plane half-spaces and the aliased plane transform, bounding-volume conventions, Rectangle edge ownership, Color counts and packing, curve extrapolation, split exception families and what the tests prove. Its counts (818 tests, 7 streams, 'no oracle'), the Ritter reading of CreateFromPoints and several defect descriptions are stale at TARGET. The site had layout and failure-map notes on the math internals page; the exact semantics, XNA comparisons and workarounds are now on the framework deep dives.

concepts.section: Geometry, Color, Curves, and C++ Value Layout
concepts.text: The complementary view to the method reference: which geometric conventions cross subsystem boundaries, which C++ layouts differ from XNA value types, and which casts or degeneracies become observable defects.
tokens: is not four floats or four bytes any more

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: XNA's vectors, colours, planes, bounds and curve keys are compact managed value types; CNA keeps their names and most operations but cannot keep their representation by spelling the same fields in C++.
tokens: whose field list is their whole representation

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: Color implements IPackedVectorT<UInt32> (virtual operations and destructor) and IEquatable<Color>, so the object carries vtable pointers ahead of its packed word and is not four raw RGBA bytes.
tokens: Two vtable pointers precede the single 32-bit packed word.
concepts.note: The Bible names only the packed-vector base; the IEquatable base adds a second vtable pointer.

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: Built-in vertex types implement IVertexType, so a vertex object cannot be uploaded by copying sizeof(T) bytes.
tokens: A vertex object cannot be uploaded by copying

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: BoundingBox, BoundingSphere, BoundingFrustum and CurveKey implement IEquatable<T>, so their field list is not their complete object representation.
tokens: The field list is not the complete object representation.

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: Vector2/3/4, Matrix, Quaternion, Plane, Ray, Point and Rectangle have no base class; their layout is simpler, but padding and object rules belong to the C++ ABI, not to the XNA contract.
tokens: Padding and object rules still belong to the C++ ABI

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: sizeof(Color) is 24 on a 64-bit host (two vtable pointers, the 4-byte word, padding); the regression test asserts only that it exceeds four bytes, and 32-bit targets are smaller.
concepts.note: Qualified as an ABI fact for 64-bit hosts, not measured here.

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: Reinterpreting a Color* as pixel bytes reads or overwrites the vtable pointer even though the packed value is little-endian RGBA.
tokens: Reinterpreting a Color* as pixel bytes reads or overwrites a vtable pointer.

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: GetBackBufferData for Color reads native bytes into a temporary byte vector and constructs Color(r, g, b, a) per pixel.

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit
concepts.text: Texture3D and TextureCube apply the same conversion rule, unpacking Color arrays to plain RGBA bytes.

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit

concepts.section: The value-type resemblance has a hard limit

concepts.section: GPU streams are a second, plain-data representation
concepts.text: The graphics core keeps a parallel internal stream layer in BuiltInVertexStreams.hpp whose structs have no virtual base and whose sizes and member offsets are compile-time asserted.

concepts.section: GPU streams are a second, plain-data representation
concepts.text: Stream sizes: PositionColor 16, PositionTexture 20, PositionColorTexture 24, PositionNormalTexture 32, PositionNormalTangentTexture 48, PositionNormalTextureSkinned 52, PositionNormalTangentTextureSkinned 68 bytes; TARGET adds three PBR/glTF streams of 60, 76 and 80 bytes.
concepts.note: Bible lists 7 streams; TARGET has 10 (three internal PBR/glTF layouts added).

concepts.section: GPU streams are a second, plain-data representation
concepts.text: Every built-in VertexDeclaration takes its stride from the matching stream struct (sizeof and offsetof), not from the public vertex class.

concepts.section: GPU streams are a second, plain-data representation
concepts.text: Conversion is an explicit Pack() step: positions and texture coordinates are copied as floats, Color contributes only its four channel bytes.

issues.text: BoundingSphere::Contains(Vector3) returns Intersects for a point exactly on the surface; XNA 4.0 returns Contains only for d^2 < r^2 and Disjoint otherwise (never Intersects).

BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingSphere) tests d^2 <= (R - r)^2, which loses the sign of R - r, so a larger argument sphere enclosing this one is reported as Contains (e.g. radius 1 containing a concentric radius 5); XNA tests R - r >= d and answers Intersects. Ported from FNA.

BoundingFrustum::Intersects(BoundingBox) and Intersects(BoundingSphere) are Contains(...) != Disjoint, a conservative per-plane test that reports true for volumes beside a frustum edge or corner; XNA 4.0 uses an exact GJK query. BoundingBox/BoundingSphere::Intersects(frustum) and the engine-layer culling helpers inherit it.
issues.evidence: modules/math/src/BoundingFrustum.cpp (Intersects overloads, Contains); XNA 4.0 BoundingFrustum.Intersects(ref BoundingBox/ref BoundingSphere) with Gjk

issues.text: BoundingFrustum::Intersects(Plane) classifies corners with Plane::IntersectsPoint, so a corner exactly on the plane counts as Intersecting; XNA counts a zero distance as Back, so a frustum touching a plane from behind is Back in XNA and Intersecting in CNA.
Point declares operator+, -, * and / (component-wise, no divide-by-zero guard), which XNA 4.0's Point does not have, without the CNAEXT marker, so CNA_STRICT_XNA_API does not flag them.

Color::FromNonPremultiplied(intcs r, g, b, a) computes r * a / 255 in 32-bit int; XNA multiplies in 64-bit long and clamps, so arguments whose product exceeds INT_MAX overflow (undefined behaviour) in CNA.
Plane::Transform(Plane, Matrix) transposes the inverse in place through a non-alias-safe Matrix::Transpose. (verified and published by B1; stated on the WP04 pages as a plain scoped fact)
BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingFrustum) never returns Disjoint. (verified and published by B1; stated on the WP04 pages as a plain scoped fact)
BoundingBox::Contains(BoundingFrustum) never returns Disjoint; corner-0 fallback. (verified and published by B1; stated on the WP04 pages as a plain scoped fact)
BoundingFrustum::Intersects(Ray) classifies only the origin; throws on a boundary origin. (verified and published by B1; stated on the WP04 pages as a plain scoped fact)
PlaneIntersectionType Doxygen swaps Front and Back. (verified and published by B1; stated on the WP04 pages as a plain scoped fact)
